chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Siyaba from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:
Backbiting (ghiba) includes saying about your brother that which Allah has concealed, and slander (buhtan) includes saying about your brother that which is not true of him.

key_terms.البهتان: Buhtan (slander/calumny): attributing a false characteristic or deed to a fellow Muslim
key_terms.الغيبة: Ghiba (backbiting): mentioning a true but concealed fault of a fellow Muslim in their absence

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between backbiting (ghiba) and slander (buhtan) in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines two serious social sins: backbiting (ghiba) and slander (buhtan). Backbiting is revealing about a fellow Muslim something true that Allah had concealed for that person, while slander is attributing to a Muslim something that is entirely false. This distinction was important for the early Muslim community as both sins violate the dignity and honor of a believer.
